newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends broadly lower on fungus, EU move.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends broadly lower on fungus, EU move.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended broadly lower and set new contract lows amid a host of bearish inputs, traders said.

The discovery of karnal bunt fungus in Tennessee wheat pulled prices lower early. More pressure came as the EU raised soft wheat refunds to a maximum of 19.98 Ecus per tonne. A sharp drop in CBOT soybeans provided spillover weakness.
KCBT wheat also weakened as the cash market showed some softness, traders said.
KCBT wheat settled unchanged to 10-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down 10-3/4 cents at $4.06. KCBT Dec wheat set a new contract low at $4.01-3/4.
"Technically, we knew we were going to make a run to $4 per bushel," a trader said. "We just didn't know it was going to come this fast."
Traders said E D & F Man International sold 3.8 million Dec bushels and 1.4 million March. Man also bear-spread at least two million March/Dec at 18 to 19 cents and bought 2.5 million March outright.
CIS bull-spread two million Dec/March bushels at 19 to 20 cents. CIS also bought three million Dec, 1.6 million March and 1.3 million July. General Mills bought two million Dec.
The Dec/March spread traded early at 21-1/2 cents but narrowed throughout the session, closing at 19-1/2 cents.
